A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VA/AlignedWVA research. All pages, including appendices, are readable, and the text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MTEB evaluations, LongBench-v2 segment-matching and probing experiments, and embedding fine-tuning results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds internal-signal, layer-range, model-size, runtime, and Qwen-3 fine-tuning evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 6.1 revises the specified GQA construction: WVA averages last-token attention weights across query heads before weighting value vectors, whereas v1 identifies WVA with attention-head outputs generally. Section 6.2 specifies extracting AlignedWVA after the output projection. This changes the reported GQA procedure; the core VA pooling and fine-tuning objective remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 14 MTEB tasks, LongBench-v2 experiments, and stated fine-tuning data. The additions vary representations and model configurations or measure runtime on the existing SciDocsRR dataset; they introduce no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 8 expands comparisons beyond hidden-state methods by evaluating query, key, and activation aggregation against VA. Table 2 also adds VA (PromptEOL) as a control and includes Qwen-3 VA in the weighted-aggregation comparison. These substantially broaden the alternatives tested while retaining the established baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds systematic layer-interval configurations, Qwen3 backbone sizes from 0.6B through 14B, Qwen-3 fine-tuning comparisons, and a controlled runtime/memory protocol. Existing benchmark splits and metrics remain unchanged. Appendix G's new 50–85% layer recommendation is not reconciled with Section 4.2's retained model-specific layer lists, so it cannot be treated as an established replacement setting for all results.

E4.justification: Appendices G–J add substantive analyses of layer-range sensitivity, alternative internal signals, backbone scaling, and computational efficiency. Table 2 adds a prompted-VA control that helps separate prompting from weighting. These extend v1's layer-wise and continuation-probing analyses across several additional questions.

E5.justification: Figure 8's variance bands are unchanged. v2 introduces no new seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures; the added tables report point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces Qwen-3 WVA averages for LT, PromptEOL, and FutureEOL from 37.30/40.71/41.88 to 32.92/45.02/45.66 alongside the revised GQA specification. Its LLaMA-2 VA row changes from 50.94 to 52.25, now matching Table 1's selected-layer rather than half-layer results. Table 6 adds Qwen-3 fine-tuning outcomes, and Tables 7–10 add substantial results, including approximately 279 versus 40 encoding minutes for MetaEOL and AlignedWVA. These are revised or newly reported results, not uniformly comparable performance gains.

T1.justification: Definition D.1 drops its explicit positive-temperature condition, τ > 0, while retaining τ in the formulas; that condition remains in Definition D.2. This is a small deletion in formal specification. The truth-condition definitions, Hypothesis 3.1, and InfoNCE-equivalence proposition and proof otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about value-based semantics, VA, AlignedWVA performance and efficiency, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning. The additional experiments support existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: New appendix discussions interpret deeper-layer robustness, values as content carriers versus query/key matching, and scaling through stronger backbone representations. Section 6.2 removes the specific explanation that GQA alignment projects pooled values into a higher-dimensional, more expressive space. Appendix F also removes its detailed compact-embedding interpretation for Qwen3-8B, while retaining the underlying results.

D1.justification: Section 6 provides more explicit GQA weighting and post-projection extraction instructions. Appendix J documents the new timing experiment's 89,133 samples, batch size 1, NVIDIA H20 GPU, PyTorch 2.9.1+cu128, and eager-attention backend. These are focused technical additions rather than a general reproducibility overhaul.

R1.justification: Appendix G newly connects the proposed layer-range heuristic to compression valleys and deeper-layer task information in already-cited work by Queipo-de-Llano et al. and Wang et al. The bibliography adds no new works; publication-year and venue updates are metadata changes.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized Section 6 rewrites, corrects the Table 3 reference and erroneous descriptions of VA as hidden-state pooling, expands the impact statement, and adds an affiliation and acknowledgements. Appendices G–J extend the document without substantially reorganizing or rewriting the retained narrative.

P2.justification: Tables 7–10 add distinct displays for layer intervals, internal signals, model scaling, and runtime/memory, substantially expanding the empirical tabular presentation. Tables 2 and 6 gain rows, and Figure 9 moves within the appendix. Existing figure content and the overall two-column format remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added signal comparisons, sensitivity analyses, and measured runtime advantage strengthen the evidence behind existing design and efficiency claims. Corrected VA descriptions and more explicit GQA instructions also improve clarity. These gains are limited by the unreconciled 50–85% layer recommendation in Appendix G versus the model-specific defaults retained in Section 4.2, which introduces reproducibility ambiguity. Overall, v2 provides a useful but limited quality improvement.
